label: History
value: Mrs. Allan arrived in Avonlea five years prior as a new bride
unit: Mrs. Allan arrived in Avonlea five years prior as a new bride alongside her minister husband, having grown up as a self-described mischievous girl who was a dunce at geometry. During a tea party at Green Gables, she graciously comforted a mortified Anne after the girl mistakenly flavored a cake with liniment, taking an interest in Anne's flower garden instead. In times of tragedy and reflection, Mrs. Allan provided comforting counsel to Anne following Matthew's death and later shared a walk home with her to discuss teaching, life choices, and the value of friendship.

unit: Mrs. Allan serves as a valued friend and mentor to Anne Shirley, offering gentle guidance and acting as a comforting presence. Their friendship deepens early on when Mrs. Allan kindly comforts Anne after a embarrassing baking mishap involving a liniment-flavored cake, and Mrs. Allan later provides spiritual and emotional support following Matthew's death. Over the years, the two share meaningful conversations on topics ranging from teaching ideals and life choices to memory and the enduring value of friendship.

label: Appearance
value: Anne is a tall girl.
unit: Anne is a tall and slender girl with a milk-white skin, a slim throat, and a pointed, freckled face. She possesses solemn, luminous gray eyes, which are sometimes described as gray-green, set above a pointed chin and a nicely shaped, freckled nose. Her hair, which friends call auburn, is notably red and has been worn in long braids, shingled closely, and left unbraided in a torrent of brightness. She has an expressive face with delicate features, pale cheeks that faintly flush with pink, and an overall bright, animated appearance.

label: History
value: Anne Shirley was born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Born in Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, Anne Shirley was orphaned as an infant and raised by Mrs. Thomas, Mrs. Hammond, and an asylum before Matthew Cuthbert brought her to Green Gables [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F6, F9]. Upon her arrival, she broke into tears when Marilla Cuthbert expressed shock that she was not a boy, though Marilla ultimately decided to raise her [S1, S3]. In Avonlea, Anne swore eternal friendship with Diana Barry, a bond that survived a temporary ban after Anne accidentally served Diana home-made currant wine [S9, S15, S17]. At school, she smashed her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head after he taunted her red hair, igniting a prolonged academic rivalry [S13, S40]. Following Matthew's sudden death, Anne gave up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Marilla's failing eyes, and teach locally, reconciling with Gilbert after he gave up the Avonlea school for her [S42, S43]. While teaching, she helped found the Village Improvement Society and convinced Marilla to take in the orphaned twins Davy and Dora Keith [S45, S51]. Later, after earning her degree at Redmond College, she rejected a proposal from Roy Gardner before accepting Gilbert's proposal in Hester Gray's garden [S115, S117]. The couple married and moved to Four Winds Harbor, where Anne formed deep friendships with Captain Jim and their tragic neighbor Leslie Moore [S120, S121, S130]. After the heartbreaking loss of her first baby, Joyce, Anne gave birth to a healthy son, James Matthew [S138, S140, S153]. Eventually, after Captain Jim's peaceful death, Anne and Gilbert prepared to move to the Glen, comforted that Leslie and her new husband would purchase their beloved home [S158, S159].

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I’m better at looking after children, though. I’ve had so much experience at that. It’s such a pity you haven’t any here for me to look after."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: “I think he’s lovely,” said Anne reproachfully. “He is so very sympathetic. He didn’t mind how much I talked—he seemed to like it. I felt that he was a kindred spirit as soon as ever I saw him.”

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Oh, I don’t mean that sort of a name. I mean just a name you gave it yourself. Didn’t you give it a name? May I give it one then? May I call it—let me see—Bonny would do—may I call it Bonny while I’m here? Oh, do let me!"

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "Pretty well. I imagine a good deal, and that helps to pass the time. Of course, it’s rather lonesome. But then, I may as well get used to that."

label: Quote
value: Anne Shirley said: "I don’t get cross about other things; but I’m so tired of being twitted about my hair and it just makes me boil right over. Do you suppose my hair will really be a handsome auburn when I grow up?"

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina never attended college.
unit: Aunt Jamesina never attended college, as she was born a month after her father drowned at sea. Later in life, she moved into Patty's Place to act as a chaperone for Anne Shirley and her friends, bringing along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat. She took an easygoing approach to chaperoning the young women and frequently shared conversations with them regarding their lives and old suitors. As the girls progressed through their years at Redmond, she continued to live alongside them at Patty's Place, offering company and comfort during their academic studies, romantic developments, and graduation preparations.

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "She couldn’t take Joseph with her so she begged me to take him. I really couldn’t refuse. He’s a beautiful cat—that is, his disposition is beautiful. She called him Joseph because his coat is of many colors."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Kittens have to be drowned, I admit, or the world would be overrun. But no decent, grown-up cat should be done to death—unless he sucks eggs."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: “I suppose you feel kind of, sorry” said Aunt Jamesina. “The teens are such a nice part of life. I’m glad I’ve never gone out of them myself.”

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Well, I hope so, Anne. I do hope so, because I love her. But I can’t understand her—she beats me. She isn’t like any of the girls I ever knew, or any of the girls I was myself."

label: Quote
value: Aunt Jamesina said: "Yes, in my soul. But I’ll admit my legs aren’t as young as yours. You go and get some fresh air, Anne. You look pale lately."

label: History
value: Charlotta the Fourth was born with the given name Leonora.
unit: Born with the given name Leonora, Charlotta the Fourth worked as a young handmaiden for Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge. She assisted her mistress during visits from Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, and later confided her concerns to Anne regarding Miss Lavendar's despondency. During Stephen Irving's visit, Charlotta anxiously waited in the kitchen with Anne before happily witnessing the couple's reconciliation in the garden. She continued to offer commentary as Anne helped plan Miss Lavendar's wedding, and she later attended Anne's own wedding at Green Gables after eventually marrying a bricklayer named Tom.

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: “Oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am,” she breathed, “I peeked from the kitchen window . . . and he’s awful handsome . . . and just the right age for Miss Lavendar. And oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, do you think it would be much harm to listen at the door?”

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "But I’m sure I shan’t sleep a blessed wink, Miss Shirley, ma’am, for fear that something’ll go wrong at the last minute . . . the cream won’t whip . . . or Mr. Irving’ll have a stroke and not be able to come."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "but there’s so much to do yet . . . and oh, Miss Shirley, ma’am, I’m skeered it’s going to rain and I wish you’d get up and tell me you think it ain’t."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: "it’s plain to be seen you and Miss Lavendar have got a secret and I think, begging your pardon if I’m too forward, Miss Shirley, ma’am, that it’s real mean not to tell me when we’ve all been such chums."

label: Quote
value: Charlotta said: “No, I can understand that,” said Charlotta. “A wedding ain’t poetry. Why, Miss Shirley, ma’am, you’re crying! What for?”

label: History
value: Cornelia Bryant grew up as an only child for eight years.
unit: Cornelia Bryant grew up as an only child for eight years, longing for siblings, before having a brother who died in his early twenties; ten years prior to her visits with Anne Blythe, she won a prize for lemon pies at the Charlottetown Exhibition. Miss Cornelia became a frequent visitor at Anne and Gilbert Blythe's home in Four Winds, entertaining Anne with her sharp-tongued opinions and village gossip while recounting the tragic life story of their neighbor, Leslie Moore. She attended Christmas dinner with the Blythes and periodically visited to engage in lively debates on theology, gossip, and local news alongside Captain Jim and Susan Baker. When Gilbert proposed a medical operation for Dick Moore, Cornelia initially confronted Anne in anger over his intervention, though she accepted the decision once it was made. She was later amazed when Anne shared a letter from Leslie revealing that Dick was actually his cousin George Moore, making Leslie a free woman, prompting Cornelia to subtly suggest informing Owen Ford of Leslie's freedom. Eventually, Cornelia shocked her friends by announcing her upcoming marriage to Marshall Elliott, taking Gilbert's playful teasing about her sudden engagement in good stride.

unit: Cornelia Bryant grew up as an only child for eight years, longing for siblings, before having a brother who died in his early twenties; ten years prior to her visits with Anne Blythe, she won a prize for lemon pies at the Charlottetown Exhibition. Miss Cornelia became a frequent visitor at Anne and Gilbert Blythe's home in Four Winds, entertaining Anne with her sharp-tongued opinions and village gossip while recounting the tragic life story of their neighbor, Leslie Moore. She attended Christmas dinner with the Blythes and periodically visited to engage in lively debates on theology, gossip, and local news alongside Captain Jim and Susan Baker. When Gilbert proposed a medical operation for Dick Moore, Cornelia initially confronted Anne in anger over his intervention, though she accepted the decision once it was made. She was later amazed when Anne shared a letter from Leslie revealing that Dick was actually his cousin George Moore, making Leslie a free woman, prompting Cornelia to subtly suggest informing Owen Ford of Leslie's freedom. Eventually, Cornelia shocked her friends by announcing her upcoming marriage to Marshall Elliott, taking Gilbert's playful teasing about her sudden engagement in good stride.

label: Quote
value: Cornelia Bryant said: "I have the Methodist minister’s word for it—if you call THAT proof. Robert Baxter told me the same thing too, but I admit THAT isn’t evidence. Robert Baxter isn’t often known to tell the truth."

label: Quote
value: Cornelia Bryant said: “I am sure I hope so,” said Miss Cornelia, none too hopefully. “But speaking of the devil, I am positive that Billy Booth is possessed by him now. Have you heard of Billy’s latest performance?”

label: Quote
value: Cornelia Bryant said: "You always look as cool as a cucumber, Anne, dearie. Do I smell cherry pie? If I do, ask me to stay to tea. Haven’t tasted a cherry pie this summer. My cherries have all been stolen by those scamps of Gilman boys from the Glen."

label: Quote
value: Cornelia Bryant said: "There’s a great change come over her lately. She laughs and jokes like a girl, and from her talk I gather she’s here real often."

label: Quote
value: Cornelia Bryant said: "Anne, do you mean to tell me it’s true what I’ve heard—that Dr. Blythe has told Leslie Dick can be cured, and that she is going to take him to Montreal to have him operated on?"

label: History
value: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster.
unit: Diana Barry was named by a schoolmaster who boarded with her family when she was born. In her youth, she met Anne Shirley in the garden at Orchard Slope, where they solemnly vowed eternal friendship. Their bond faced an early test when Mrs. Barry temporarily forbade Diana from playing with Anne, but Diana later rushed to Green Gables for help when her sister Minnie May fell ill with severe croup. After Anne successfully treated Minnie May, Diana's mother restored the girls' friendship in gratitude. As their school years progressed, Diana gave Anne Christmas gifts, formed a story club with her, and excitedly brought the newspaper to Green Gables announcing Anne's top score on the entrance exams. She actively joined Anne in community affairs, canvassing for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, accompanying Anne on outings, and aiding in hosting special guests. When Anne departed for Redmond College, Diana expressed deep concern about her leaving, though the two maintained their close connection during holidays and summer breaks. Diana read and gave feedback on Anne's writing, and later confided her engagement to Fred Wright. Anne helped Diana prepare for her wedding, where they fondly remembered their childhood vows before Diana married Fred. Eventually, Diana welcomed a newborn baby, which Anne came to visit.

In her youth, she met Anne Shirley in the garden at Orchard Slope, where they solemnly vowed eternal friendship. Their bond faced an early test when Mrs. Barry temporarily forbade Diana from playing with Anne, but Diana later rushed to Green Gables for help when her sister Minnie May fell ill with severe croup. After Anne successfully treated Minnie May, Diana's mother restored the girls' friendship in gratitude. As their school years progressed, Diana gave Anne Christmas gifts, formed a story club with her, and excitedly brought the newspaper to Green Gables announcing Anne's top score on the entrance exams. She actively joined Anne in community affairs, canvassing for the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, accompanying Anne on outings, and aiding in hosting special guests. When Anne departed for Redmond College, Diana expressed deep concern about her leaving, though the two maintained their close connection during holidays and summer breaks. Diana read and gave feedback on Anne's writing, and later confided her engagement to Fred Wright. Anne helped Diana prepare for her wedding, where they fondly remembered their childhood vows before Diana married Fred. Eventually, Diana welcomed a newborn baby, which Anne came to visit.

value: Diana Barry said: "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Those Pye girls are cheats all round,” said Diana indignantly, as they climbed the fence of the main road. “Gertie Pye actually went and put her milk bottle in my place in the brook yesterday. Did you ever? I don’t speak to her now.”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “I don’t believe he’ll find the doctor at Carmody,” sobbed Diana. “I know that Dr. Blair went to town and I guess Dr. Spencer would go too. Young Mary Joe never saw anybody with croup and Mrs. Lynde is away. Oh, Anne!”

label: Quote
value: Diana Barry said: “Everything went off very well,” said Diana practically. “I guess we must have made as much as ten dollars. Mind you, Mr. Allan is going to send an account of it to the Charlottetown papers.”

label: History
value: Dick originally spent his summers sailing.
unit: Dick originally spent his summers sailing and his winters clerking in his father's store before he died of yellow fever in Cuba thirteen years prior. After he went missing, his cousin George Moore—who had suffered a brain injury that caused severe memory loss—was mistaken for Dick and brought home by Captain Jim. This man lived with Dick's wife, Leslie, on the West place through the winter, until Gilbert suggested a surgical operation in Montreal to relieve the pressure on his brain. Following the successful surgery, it was revealed that the man was not Dick at all, but his cousin George.

label: Personality
value: Dora is a quiet child.
unit: Dora is a quiet, lovely, and well-behaved child who is often seen as a model of proper behavior. Characterized by a prim and demure manner, she speaks when spoken to and remains composed even in tense situations. She is exceptionally neat, faithful, and industrious, taking joy in helping with small tasks suited to her hands. In her learning and chores, she works carefully, systematically, and dispassionately, reciting her lessons meekly like a machine. Considered placid, sensible, and unusually careful for her age, her predictable nature has been likened to a book where every page is identical. As she grows, she maintains her quiet disposition and develops into a womanly and helpful individual.

label: History
value: Dora Keith moved to Green Gables
unit: Dora Keith moved to Green Gables with her twin brother Davy, though she was soon pushed into a pigpen by him and later locked in a toolhouse as part of one of his pranks. Her stay at Green Gables became permanent after her uncle, Richard Keith, died and left money in trust for the twins. While attending school, Dora was once frightened by a classmate's stories about a ghost relative, and on another occasion, she was coerced by Davy into skipping Sunday School to go fishing. Over time, she continued living at Green Gables alongside Marilla, Mrs. Lynde, and Davy, joining them in welcoming Anne back for visits and eventually celebrating Anne and Gilbert's wedding.

label: History
value: Gilbert Blythe grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Gilbert Blythe grew up in Avonlea, where he once taunted Anne Shirley at school, resulting in her smashing a slate over his head and spurning his apologies. During their school years, he entered into a fierce academic rivalry with Anne, though he saved her life on the pond when her boat sank. The two tied academically for their Entrance exams, with Gilbert winning the school medal, but he generously relinquished the Avonlea teaching post so Anne could stay close to Green Gables. During their time teaching, Gilbert and Anne reconciled into close friends and discussed school corporal punishment as well as their future plans. He later attended Redmond College, where he led the Freshmen to victory in the annual rush, took High Honors in Classics, and won the Cooper Prize. Although Anne initially rejected his marriage proposal in college, Gilbert later confessed his enduring love for her in Hester Gray's garden, and she accepted. After their wedding in the orchard at Green Gables, Gilbert moved with Anne to Four Winds Harbor to begin his medical career. Following the tragic loss of their firstborn child, Joyce, Gilbert insisted that his colleague tell Leslie Moore about a potential brain operation for her husband, which led to the revelation that the man was actually Leslie's cousin. After taking over his great-uncle's medical practice at Glen St. Mary, Gilbert welcomed a healthy baby boy, James Matthew, with Anne. Following the death of their friend Captain Jim, Gilbert proposed purchasing the Morgan place in the Glen to better accommodate their growing family.

label: History
value: Harrison spent part of his boyhood on Prince Edward Island
unit: Harrison spent part of his boyhood on Prince Edward Island and lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before moving to Avonlea as a bachelor. Shortly after becoming Anne Shirley's neighbor, he angrily confronted her when her cow strayed into his oatfield, but the two forged an unexpected friendship after Anne accidentally sold his Jersey cow and came to his house to confess. Their bond grew despite Harrison's skepticism of her teaching methods and his refusal to contribute to her village improvement society. When a violent hail storm struck Avonlea, Harrison lost Ginger, a parrot given to him by his late brother. Following a rumor about his remarriage, Harrison was unexpectedly reunited with his long-estranged wife, Emily; he explained to Anne that their past separation had been caused by household nagging and his late parrot. Later, Harrison was among those Anne consulted for feedback when she wrote her short story, 'Averil's Atonement'.

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Sorry, miss! Sorry isn’t going to help matters any. You’d better go and look at the havoc that animal has made in my oats . . . trampled them from center to circumference, miss."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: “Who? Mrs. Lynde? Don’t you tell me I’m like that old gossip,” said Mr. Harrison irritably. “I’m not . . . not a bit. What have you got in that box?”

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I don’t, that’s a fact, and I’m mighty fond of it, too. I’m much obliged to you. It looks good on top. I hope it’s good all the way through."

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "Well, I’ll tell you what, miss, you must help me eat it. I’ll put the kettle on and we’ll have a cup of tea. How will that do?"

label: Quote
value: Harrison said: "I see you haven’t much confidence in my ability to make tea. You’re wrong . . . I can brew up as good a jorum of tea as you ever drank. But go ahead yourself. Fortunately it rained last Sunday, so there’s plenty of clean dishes."

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea.
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school, where she joined a story club with her classmates Anne, Diana, and Ruby. She later attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne and Ruby. On the final day of their school term, Jane was brought to tears during her teacher's farewell speech and had to borrow a handkerchief from her brother. Later, Jane attended a charity concert at the White Sands Hotel, traveling to the event and returning in a carriage driven by her brother Billy. After earning her teaching certificate at Queen's, she taught at Newbridge school, earning a spot on the Inspector's Roll of Honor, before eventually resigning from her teaching position in Avonlea to teach on the western prairies. While living in Avonlea, Jane actively participated in the local Village Improvement Society and joined her friends for outings, including exploring a hidden garden. She also personally delivered a marriage proposal to Anne on behalf of her brother Billy, though Anne rejected the unromantic offer, leading Jane to react coldly. Jane eventually married a wealthy millionaire and went to Europe for her wedding tour.

label: History
value: Janet Sweet was a pleasant landlady
unit: Janet Sweet was a pleasant landlady living at Wayside in Valley Road who lost her sister Anne when her sister was young. For twenty years, she was courted by a quiet admirer named John Douglas, who visited her regularly without ever proposing. After being encouraged by her boarder Anne to take a stand, Janet briefly rejected John's escort after a prayer meeting, though Anne quickly intervened to reconcile them. Following the death of John's mother, John proposed to Janet and explained that he had been bound by a secret promise to his mother to wait until her passing before he could marry.

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "If she wasn’t—but she is. So we mustn’t speak evil of her. But I’m happy at last, Anne. And I wouldn’t have minded waiting so long a bit if I’d only known why."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "Oh, she does. She’s told me time and again that she’d love to see John settled before her time comes. She’s always giving him hints—you heard her yourself the other day. I thought I’d ha’ gone through the floor."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I couldn’t,” said poor Janet pathetically. “You see, Anne, I’ve always been awful fond of John. He might just as well keep coming as not, for there was never anybody else I’d want, so it didn’t matter.”

label: Quote
value: Janet said: "No, I guess not. I was afraid to try, anyway, for fear he’d think I meant it and just go. I suppose I’m a poor-spirited creature, but that is how I feel. And I can’t help it."

label: Quote
value: Janet said: “I dunno,” said Janet hopelessly. “I dunno if I could ever get up enough spunk. Things have drifted so long. But I’ll think it over.”

Shortly after his mother's passing, John immediately proposed to Janet and explained the reason for his long silence.

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: “I’m afraid my imagination is a little rusty—it’s so long since I used it,” she said. “I dare say your claim to sympathy is just as strong as mine. It all depends on the way we look at it. Sit down here and tell me about yourself.”

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: “I’ve made up my mind to stay simply for the sake of getting better acquainted with that Anne-girl,” she said frankly. “She amuses me, and at my time of life an amusing person is a rarity.”

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Remember, you Anne-girl, when you come to town you’re to visit me and I’ll put you in my very sparest spare-room bed to sleep."

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Oh, I must, hey? I rather think Diana did her share of the jumping at least. Such carryings on in a respectable house!"

label: Quote
value: Josephine Barry said: "Her husband was a British officer, and she is very careful what sort of boarders she takes. Anne will not meet with any objectionable persons under her roof. The table is good, and the house is near the Academy, in a quiet neighborhood."

label: Anne Shirley
value: Josephine Barry and Anne Shirley first met.
unit: Josephine Barry and Anne Shirley first met under tense circumstances when Anne unwittingly jumped into the bed where Miss Barry was sleeping during a sleepover at Diana's house. After Anne bravely took full responsibility and apologized to save Diana's music lessons from being canceled, Miss Barry became deeply amused by her and the two developed a close friendship. Over the years, Anne became Miss Barry's prime favorite, visiting her for Sunday dinners and church, and Miss Barry ultimately left Anne a thousand-dollar legacy in her will to help fund her college education.

label: History
value: Judson Parker was a voter.
unit: Judson Parker was a voter who consistently supported Grant. When he planned to rent his fences to a medicine company for painted advertisements, a committee of young women from the Village Improvement Society tried unsuccessfully to dissuade him. However, after Anne Shirley accidentally witnessed him receiving a political bribe from Jerry Corcoran, Judson agreed to drop the advertisement plan to prevent her from exposing him and ruining his reputation.

label: Personality
value: Leslie Moore is a clever woman.
unit: Leslie Moore is a clever, resolute, and determined woman who has strong ideals of duty. Known to be cold and proud since the day of her marriage, she nevertheless retains a youthful side, occasionally laughing and joking like a girl. Despite her acknowledged beauty, she deeply hates it, while intensely desiring to experience motherhood. Her practical and personal ambitions include earning money to shingle her house's roof in the fall and traveling to Montreal to pursue a career in nursing to make what she can of her life.

label: History
value: Leslie Moore was her father's favorite as a child.
unit: As a child, Leslie Moore was her father's favorite and endured significant trauma, witnessing her brother's fatal accident at twelve and discovering her father hanged two years later. After attending Queen's Academy—completing two years of work in a single year to earn her teaching certificate—she returned home to teach at the Glen school. Inheriting money from her grandmother, she married at sixteen. Later living as Anne Shirley's neighbor, she befriended Anne and Gilbert Blythe, though she initially harbored envy toward Anne's happiness until the two reconciled after the death of Anne's first child. When writer Owen Ford visited the area to adapt Captain Jim's life story into a book, Leslie spent the summer with him and Anne's circle, ultimately confessing her love for Owen to Anne after his initial departure. Later, Gilbert suggested a surgery that might restore her husband Dick's memory, and Leslie financed a trip to Montreal for the operation; the procedure revealed the man was actually Dick's cousin, George Moore, leaving her free. She eventually returned to Green Gables to assist Anne, where Owen returned to declare his love, which she joyfully accepted. After Captain Jim's death, Leslie eased Anne's sorrow over moving by revealing that she and Owen intended to buy Anne's beloved house of dreams as a summer home.

label: Personality
value: Marilla Cuthbert is a middle-aged woman.
unit: A middle-aged woman of rigid conscience and sober step, Marilla Cuthbert is characteristically stern, practical, and sensible. She is undemonstrative and repressed by nature, viewing open displays of deep emotion as unseemly and often feeling reluctant to show any emotional weakness. When communicating with children, she is prone to being crisp and curt, strongly favoring moral lessons and regularly admonishing poor table manners. Despite her strictness, she harbors extreme pride in Anne, whom she resolves to educate well so the girl is fitted to earn her own living. Marilla is also known for specific domestic skills, such as making round, braided mats and brewing celebrated homemade currant wine.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables for sixty years.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert lived at Green Gables for sixty years, having spent a cramped childhood in which she kept still when told to and harbored hidden dreams [F3, F4, F5]. In her youth, she refused to forgive John Blythe after a quarrel, a decision that left her with lingering regret [F1]. Desiring help on the farm, Marilla and her brother Matthew set out to adopt an orphan boy, but they were shocked when a girl named Anne arrived instead [S1, S3]. Though Marilla initially insisted on returning Anne, her pity for the girl's past led her to keep and raise her [S5, S6]. Over the years, Marilla strictly educated Anne, guided her through childhood misadventures, and privately grew deeply fond of her [S7, S9, S10, S28]. She supported Anne's academic ambitions at Queen's Academy, but after Matthew suddenly died and her own failing sight threatened Green Gables, Marilla was saved from selling the property when Anne chose to stay home and teach [S37, S44, S45]. To enable Anne to attend college later, Marilla took in her sick relative's twins, Davy and Dora, and invited Rachel Lynde to live with them [S53, S54, S74]. Years later, after raising Anne and helping her prepare for marriage to John Blythe's son Gilbert, Marilla saw Anne off to her new home [F6, S88, S89]. Marilla eventually traveled to Four Winds to celebrate Christmas with Anne and Gilbert, marking the first time in her life she ate a Christmas dinner away from Green Gables [F8, S90].

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I’d never dream of taking a girl to bring up. I wonder at Mrs. Alexander Spencer for doing it. But there, she wouldn’t shrink from adopting a whole orphan asylum if she took it into her head."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "I don’t feel as if I wanted any more children to look after than I’ve got at present. You’re problem enough in all conscience. What’s to be done with you I don’t know. Matthew is a most ridiculous man."

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: “There, there, Marilla, you can have your own way,” said Matthew reassuringly. “Only be as good and kind to her as you can without spoiling her. I kind of think she’s one of the sort you can do anything with if you only get her to love you.”

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "Matthew Cuthbert, I’m astonished at you. You know that Anne’s behavior was dreadful, and yet you take her part! I suppose you’ll be saying next thing that she oughtn’t to be punished at all!"

label: Quote
value: Marilla Cuthbert said: "She’ll have her meals regular, and I’ll carry them up to her myself. But she’ll stay up there until she’s willing to apologize to Mrs. Lynde, and that’s final, Matthew."

label: History
value: Marshall Elliott was a noted dancer in his youth.
unit: In his youth, Marshall Elliott was a noted dancer. After taking a long-standing political vow that left him strangely bearded, he encountered Anne and Gilbert Shirley along the lane during their visit to Captain Jim's lighthouse. He later joined a New Year's Eve celebration at the lighthouse and danced with Leslie to Captain Jim's fiddle playing. Following an election victory for the Liberals, Marshall finally shaved off his beard.

label: Personality
value: Matthew Cuthbert is exceptionally quiet.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert is an exceptionally quiet, shy, and reticent man who hates going among strangers or into places where he might have to talk. label: History
value: Matthew Cuthbert is a quiet man.
unit: Matthew Cuthbert, a quiet man with a full soft brown beard who had a weak heart, decided alongside his sister Marilla to adopt an orphan boy to help on their farm at Green Gables. However, when he went to Bright River to pick up the child, he discovered an orphan girl named Anne had been sent instead and brought her home. Though Marilla initially insisted on sending her back, Matthew gently suggested keeping her. Over time, he offered quiet encouragement and support to Anne, secretly visiting her room to convince her to apologize to a neighbor after a punishment, surprising her with sweeties, and convincing Marilla to let her attend social events. Noticing that Anne was dressed more plainly than her peers, Matthew flusteredly attempted to purchase a dress with puffed sleeves for her, ultimately getting assistance to give her the stylish outfit and slippers for a school Christmas concert. He took great pride in Anne as she grew up, emotional over how much she meant to him and celebrating her educational successes, including her earning a spot at Queen's Academy and winning the Avery Scholarship. Shortly after Anne returned home from Queen's, Matthew suddenly collapsed and died after reading a notice regarding the failure of the Abbey Bank.

Noticing that Anne was dressed more plainly than her peers, Matthew flusteredly attempted to purchase a dress with puffed sleeves for her, ultimately getting assistance to give her the stylish outfit and slippers for a school Christmas concert. label: History
value: Owen Ford is a newspaper writer.
unit: Owen Ford is a newspaper writer and short-story author, as well as the grandson of Alice Selwyn and the local schoolmaster, who came to Four Winds to recover from a severe spell of typhoid. Upon meeting Captain Jim, Owen read the old man's life-book and received his enthusiastic permission to adapt his sea tales and memories into a novel, which Owen completed by the end of the summer. During his stay, he secretly fell deeply in love with Leslie Moore, confessing his feelings to Anne Shirley, who advised him to leave in silence due to Leslie's circumstances. After returning later, Owen declared his love to Leslie in the garden, and she joyfully returned his feelings.

label: History
value: Paul Irving was a motherless boy.
unit: Paul Irving was a motherless boy who lived down near the shore with his grandmother and only grew acquainted with his father after his mother died three years prior. As an imaginative student in Anne Shirley's classroom at Avonlea, he quickly warmed to her, cheering her up with wild orchids on her first day of teaching and sharing a composition about his imaginary rock friends at the shore. At the end of the school year, Paul joined Anne in the graveyard, where they shared their thoughts on memory, grief, and imagination. Anne later visited Paul for tea in his grandmother's absence, reassuring him regarding his imaginative nature. Later, Paul accompanied Anne to Echo Lodge, where he bonded with Miss Lavendar over their shared experiences with imaginary dream-people. Years later, he returned to Avonlea as one of the guests attending Anne's wedding to Gilbert Blythe.

label: History
value: Philippa Gordon is the daughter of a wealthy and prominent Bluenose family from Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia.
unit: Philippa Gordon, the daughter of a wealthy and prominent Bluenose family from Bolingbroke, Nova Scotia, first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant while registering as a freshman at Redmond College. She quickly included them in her social circle and confided details about her suitors, Alec and Alonzo. Later, Phil begged to join Anne and Priscilla's housekeeping arrangement at Patty's Place alongside Aunt Jamesina and Stella. Though she initially struggled to choose between her suitors, Phil fell in love with Jonas Blake, an earnest theological student, while spending a summer at a boardinghouse in Prospect Point. After Jonas proposed to her, she accepted, embracing her future as a minister's wife. She also hosted Anne in Bolingbroke for a pleasant fortnight and later comforted Anne after Anne rejected Royal Gardner's marriage proposal. Following her college graduation, Phil married Jonas in Bolingbroke. She eventually traveled to Green Gables to attend Anne's wedding, gifting her Miss Patty's china dogs for the occasion.

value: Phil Gordon said: "Girls, dear, I’m tired to death. I feel like the man without a country—or was it without a shadow? I forget which. Anyway, I’ve been packing up."

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley and later taught school in Carmody. She joined Anne, Diana, and Jane on a spring walk in the woods, where they discovered Hester Gray's forgotten garden. Priscilla later made an unexpected visit to Green Gables accompanied by the author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. Upon traveling to Kingsport to study at Redmond College, Priscilla greeted Anne at the station and brought her to their initial boardinghouse. The two girls quickly befriended fellow freshman Philippa Gordon while visiting Old St. John's Cemetery. After searching for a residence for their upcoming school year, Priscilla and Anne secured Patty's Place from Miss Patty Spofford, moving in alongside Philippa, Stella, and Aunt Jamesina. Priscilla spent part of the following summer visiting Anne in Avonlea before completing her studies and graduating from Redmond.

value: Priscilla Grant said: "It would be too good to be true. Fairy tales don’t happen nowadays. I won’t hope, Anne. The disappointment would be too awful to bear. They’re sure to want more for it than we can afford. Remember, it’s on Spofford Avenue."

label: Personality
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable woman.
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde is an exceptionally capable, farseeing, and practical woman who prides herself on being an honest judge of human nature and speaking her mind without fear or favor. Highly observant and naturally curious, she is known as an outspoken gossip who can be critical and bossy, often attempting to manage and properly bring up those around her regardless of their age. Despite her strict and matter-of-fact demeanor, she possesses a kind, generous heart, never shirking her share of work, helping the poor, and keeping a box of cookies for others. She is a pious church member deeply devoted to church affairs who believes that everything is foreordained, though she remains opposed to the higher education of women and holds dubious views regarding the propriety of fiction writing. Additionally, she loves to be asked for advice, can admit to her own mistakes, and holds a first-prize skill in making homemade butter and cheese.

value: Rachel Lynde said: "I knew there’d be trouble when Robert Bell sold his place to a New Brunswick man, that’s what. I don’t know what Avonlea is coming to, with so many strange people rushing into it. It’ll soon not be safe to go to sleep in our beds."

value: Roy Gardner was forced to leave college
unit: Roy Gardner was forced to leave college two years prior to travel abroad with his ailing, widowed mother. After returning, he rescued Anne Shirley during a November storm, fulfilling her vision of an ideal hero and sending her roses afterward. Roy began courting Anne, attending a college reception with her and arranging for his family to visit her prior to graduation. Following graduation, Roy proposed to Anne on a walk, but she realized she did not love him and rejected his proposal.

label: History
value: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea
unit: Ruby Gillis grew up in Avonlea with several older sisters who were married or courted, and she once charmed away her warts using a magic pebble from old Mary Joe. She attended school alongside Anne Shirley and joined her and other classmates in forming a story club. While attending Queen's Academy, she visited Anne with their friends to anxiously discuss their upcoming final examinations and commencement plans. Ruby later earned a teaching license and was hired to teach at Carmody school, and she also took a autumn trip to visit Boston. In a later summer, Anne and Diana visited Ruby at her home, where Ruby displayed summer clothes and aggressively denied her terminal illness. Soon after, Ruby spent an evening with Anne, tearfully confessing her fear of death and her unfulfilled dreams, before passing away peacefully in her sleep the next night.

She attended school alongside Anne Shirley and joined her and other classmates in forming a story club. While attending Queen's Academy, she visited Anne with their friends to anxiously discuss their upcoming final examinations and commencement plans. Ruby later earned a teaching license and was hired to teach at Carmody school, and she also took a autumn trip to visit Boston. In a later summer, Anne and Diana visited Ruby at her home, where Ruby displayed summer clothes and aggressively denied her terminal illness. Soon after, Ruby spent an evening with Anne, tearfully confessing her fear of death and her unfulfilled dreams, before passing away peacefully in her sleep the next night.

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: “Nor I,” said Ruby Gillis, with a shiver. “I don’t mind floating down when there’s two or three of us in the flat and we can sit up. It’s fun then. But to lie down and pretend I was dead—I just couldn’t. I’d die really of fright.”

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "There’s a concert at Carmody and a party at White Sands. Herb Spencer’s going to take me. He’s my latest. Be sure to come up tomorrow. I’m dying for a good talk with you. I want to hear all about your doings at Redmond."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Me! Why, I’m perfectly well. I never felt better in my life. Of course, that congestion last winter pulled me down a little. But just see my color. I don’t look much like an invalid, I’m sure."

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "Anne, it won’t be long now before I’ll be lying over there. You and Diana and all the rest will be going about, full of life—and I’ll be there—in the old graveyard—dead!"

label: Quote
value: Ruby Gillis said: "I’ll try. I’ll think over what you have said, and try to believe it. And you’ll come up as often as you can, won’t you, Anne?"

value: Shirley said: "Fare thee well, my beloved friend. Henceforth we must be as strangers though living side by side. But my heart will ever be faithful to thee."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: "That is all there is left in life for me, now that my friend has been ruthlessly torn from me. In school I can look at her and muse over days departed."

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “I think he has only been its nominal head for many years,” said Anne. “He is a very old man; his nephews are really at the head of the institution.”

label: Quote
value: Shirley said: “If I had been the boy you sent for,” said Anne wistfully, “I’d be able to help you so much now and spare you in a hundred ways. I could find it in my heart to wish I had been, just for that.”

value: Stella Maynard said: "I was afraid they’d come back. And then our jolly little nest here would be broken up—and we poor callow nestlings thrown out on the cruel world of boardinghouses again."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "I love Anne and I like Roy. Everybody says she is making a brilliant match, and even Mrs. Gardner thinks her charming now. It all sounds as if it were made in heaven, but I have my doubts. Make the most of that, Aunt Jamesina."

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Nothing seems worthwhile. My very thoughts are old. I’ve thought them all before. What is the use of living after all, Anne?"

label: Quote
value: Stella Maynard said: "Oh, my mind agrees with you, Anne. But my soul remains doleful and uninspired. I’m always grubby and dingy on rainy nights."

value: Stephen Irving said: “This is the one place where time stands still,” he said, looking around him with delighted eyes. “There is nothing changed about this house or garden since I was here twenty-five years ago. It makes me feel young again.”

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "I am of the opinion that we will all be glad of a bite and sup. You tell young Mrs. Doctor not to worry about a single thing—Susan is at the helm. You tell her just to think of her baby."

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "Oh, the poor lamb—the poor lamb! How can she bear it, Miss Cuthbert? I am afraid it will kill her. She has been that built up and happy, longing for that baby, and planning for it. Cannot anything be done nohow, Miss Cuthbert?"

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "I never saw one so white—they are mostly red or yallow. And it opened its big eyes as if it was months old. The little, little thing! Oh, the poor, young Mrs. Doctor!"

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "Have a good time and do not worry about the pantry. Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking. I am going to take your breakfast up to you every morning."

label: Quote
value: Susan said: "If you cannot I will not go, Mrs. Doctor, dear, Matilda’s leg to the contrary notwithstanding. I will not have you worried, and that blessed child upset in consequence, for any number of legs."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "Nephew Alec. He understands it as well as I do. Well, now, I’m real glad you asked me to stay to supper. I’m proper hungry—didn’t have much of a dinner today."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: “Oh, I do, Mistress Doctor, I do,” protested Captain Jim. “Why, I live like a king gen’rally. Last night I was up to the Glen and took home two pounds of steak. I meant to have a spanking good dinner today.”

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Jim said: "I reckon when the darkness is close to us it is a friend. But when we sorter push it away from us—divorce ourselves from it, so to speak, with lantern light—it becomes an enemy. But the fog is lifting."

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

label: v3 · Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday
value: Anne visits Phil in Bolingbroke for a fortnight.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XXI Roses of Yesterday
unit: During a pleasant fortnight visiting Phil in Bolingbroke, Anne visits her humble birthplace where the current occupant allows her to explore the house and gives her a packet of her mother's old letters. Afterward, Anne visits her parents' grave before returning to read the letters, which make her feel truly connected to them for the first time.

value: Anne returns home on the last day of school.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
unit: Anne returns home on the last day of school, emotional after Mr. Phillips's farewell speech and eager about the arrival of Avonlea's new minister, Mr. Allan, and his wife. Green Gables prepares to host the new minister and his wife for tea, with Anne making a layer cake for Mrs. Allan. However, during the tea party, Mrs. Allan and Marilla notice a strange taste in Anne's cake.

value: During tea with Mr. Allan
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXI. A New Departure in Flavorings
unit: During tea with Mr. and Mrs. Allan, Anne's homemade cake is discovered to have been accidentally flavored with anodyne liniment instead of vanilla. Mortified, Anne flees to her room, but Mrs. Allan kindly comforts her and invites her to show off her flower garden. Afterward, Anne reflects optimistically to Marilla that tomorrow is a new day free of mistakes.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death
value: Matthew collapses.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVII. The Reaper Whose Name Is Death
unit: Matthew suddenly collapses and dies after reading a notice about the failure of the Abbey Bank. After his funeral, Anne and Marilla comfort each other in their shared grief. Later, Anne talks with Mrs. Allan about finding moments of joy amidst her sorrow, and Marilla reflects on her past romantic history with Gilbert Blythe's father.

label: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
value: Marilla brings Davy and Dora Keith home to Green Gables.
chapter: v2 · VIII Marilla Adopts Twins
unit: Marilla brings the twins, Davy and Dora Keith, home to Green Gables, where Davy quickly displays his mischievous and unruly nature. Over the next few days, Davy causes trouble by dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck at church, making Dora fall into a pigpen, and hiding a toad in Marilla's bed.

label: v2 · XV The Beginning of Vacation
value: Anne finishes the school year.
chapter: v2 · XV The Beginning of Vacation
unit: Anne finishes the school year and walks to the graveyard, joining Paul Irving as they share their feelings about memory, grief, and imagination. After placing flowers on the graves, Anne meets Mrs. Allan, and they walk home together while reflecting on teaching, ideals, life choices, and the value of friendship.

label: v2 · XVII A Chapter of Accidents
value: Anne and Diana frantically decorate Green Gables
chapter: v2 · XVII A Chapter of Accidents
unit: Anne and Diana frantically decorate Green Gables and prepare a elaborate dinner for the arrival of the famous author Mrs. Morgan. However, Davy accidentally destroys the lemon pies, the guest of honor fails to arrive, and a series of mishaps ruins the meal and results in Miss Barry's expensive platter being broken. A later letter reveals Mrs. Morgan sprained her ankle, leaving Anne to reflect on her bitter disappointment.

unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

unit: At a party, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, leading to a fall that breaks Anne's ankle. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues and discuss the village hall painting project. Later, Joshua Pye paints the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with paint numbers, causing dismay among the Improvers. Despite the hideous result, public sympathy turns in favor of the Improvement Society, and the community rallies around them.

Miss Lavendar warmly invites them to stay for a imaginary tea party she had set up to combat loneliness.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

Despite the hideous result, public sympathy turns in favor of the Improvement Society, and the community rallies around them.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

Later, Joshua Pye paints the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with paint numbers, causing dismay among the Improvers. Despite the hideous result, public sympathy turns in favor of the Improvement Society, and the community rallies around them.

value: Anne walks home from school.
chapter: v2 · X Davy in Search of a Sensation
unit: After walking home from school, Anne finds Marilla panicking because Dora is missing, and the household fears she may have fallen into the well. Anne discovers Dora locked in Mr. Harrison's toolhouse and realizes Davy hid her and lied about it. When confronted, Davy tearfully apologizes after realizing lying hurts Anne, prompting Anne and Marilla to forgive his deceit while punishing him for the prank.

value: Anne is in a bad mood from a toothache.

unit: In a bad mood from a toothache, Anne accidentally causes fireworks to explode in the schoolroom and subsequently whips Anthony Pye after he puts a mouse in her desk. She goes home heartbroken over her bad day, but Marilla comforts her. The next morning, Anthony treats Anne with new respect, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that the whipping gained his approval.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

unit: Anne and her friends re-enact the story of Elaine, floating Anne down the pond in a leaky boat. label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar.
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

unit: Anne returns to teaching school, where Dora is frightened by Mirabel Cotton's stories about a ghost relative. label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

On Christmas morning, Anne is overjoyed to receive the stylish dress from Matthew as well as a pair of slippers sent by Aunt Josephine. She later wears her new outfit to the school concert, where she performs brilliantly.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne is in a bad mood from a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In a bad mood from a toothache, Anne accidentally causes fireworks to explode in the schoolroom and subsequently whips Anthony Pye after he puts a mouse in her desk. She goes home heartbroken over her bad day, but Marilla comforts her. The next morning, Anthony treats Anne with new respect, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that the whipping gained his approval.

value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar.
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

unit: At a party, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, leading to a fall that breaks Anne's ankle. unit: Anne and her friends re-enact the story of Elaine, floating Anne down the pond in a leaky boat. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXIV. A Queen’s Girl
unit: Anne prepares for Queen's Academy with help from Marilla and Matthew, who grows emotional reflecting on how much Anne means to them. Upon arriving in town, Anne adjusts to her new living arrangements and classes, feeling a mix of rivalry with Gilbert Blythe and homesickness. Her spirits are lifted when Josie Pye, Jane, and Ruby visit, bringing news that Queen's will award an Avery scholarship to Redmond College.

label: v2 · IV Different Opinions
value: Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate.
chapter: v2 · IV Different Opinions
unit: Anne, Jane, and Gilbert debate the ethics and effectiveness of corporal punishment in school teaching on the eve of the school year. Anne then visits Mr. Harrison, who also doubts her plan to rule by affection rather than the rod, leaving Anne anxious about her upcoming first day of teaching.

label: v2 · XVII A Chapter of Accidents
value: Anne and Diana frantically decorate Green Gables
chapter: v2 · XVII A Chapter of Accidents
unit: Anne and Diana frantically decorate Green Gables and prepare a elaborate dinner for the arrival of the famous author Mrs. Morgan. However, Davy accidentally destroys the lemon pies, the guest of honor fails to arrive, and a series of mishaps ruins the meal and results in Miss Barry's expensive platter being broken. A later letter reveals Mrs. Morgan sprained her ankle, leaving Anne to reflect on her bitter disappointment.

value: The girls are preparing for April exams.
chapter: v3 · Chapter XXVII Mutual Confidences
unit: While preparing for April exams at Patty's Place, the girls learn they can keep the house for another year. They discuss Phil's future as a minister's wife, and Phil turns the conversation to Anne's feelings for Roy Gardner.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

When confronted, Davy tearfully apologizes after realizing lying hurts Anne, prompting Anne and Marilla to forgive his deceit while punishing him for the prank.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues and discuss the village hall painting project. When confronted, Davy tearfully apologizes after realizing lying hurts Anne, prompting Anne and Marilla to forgive his deceit while punishing him for the prank.

unit: Anne returns to teaching school, where Dora is frightened by Mirabel Cotton's stories about a ghost relative. Later, Anne and Diana walk through the woods to go to West Grafton, but lose their way and discover Echo Lodge, the quaint stone home of Miss Lavendar Lewis and her young helper, Charlotta the Fourth. Miss Lavendar warmly invites them to stay for a imaginary tea party she had set up to combat loneliness.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

unit: Anne returns to teaching school, where Dora is frightened by Mirabel Cotton's stories about a ghost relative. Later, Anne and Diana walk through the woods to go to West Grafton, but lose their way and discover Echo Lodge, the quaint stone home of Miss Lavendar Lewis and her young helper, Charlotta the Fourth. Miss Lavendar warmly invites them to stay for a imaginary tea party she had set up to combat loneliness.

label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

value: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues and discuss the village hall painting project. Later, Joshua Pye paints the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with paint numbers, causing dismay among the Improvers. Despite the hideous result, public sympathy turns in favor of the Improvement Society, and the community rallies around them.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

label: v2 · XXIX Poetry and Prose
value: Anne prepares for college.
chapter: v2 · XXIX Poetry and Prose
unit: Anne prepares for college while helping Miss Lavendar plan her wedding, receiving visits and commentary from Paul Irving and Charlotta the Fourth. She discusses the romance of the marriage with Marilla before discovering Diana Barry and Fred Wright together in the garden. Diana later visits Green Gables to confide her engagement to Anne, leading Anne to reflect on love, change, and her own future.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
value: At a party, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Anne Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: At a party, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, leading to a fall that breaks Anne's ankle. Mr. Barry carries Anne home, prompting Marilla to realize how deeply she cares for the girl. During her seven weeks of bed rest, Anne is comforted by visitors, reflects on her mistakes, and looks forward to returning to school to meet her new teacher, Miss Stacy.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVI. The Glory and the Dream

unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues and discuss the village hall painting project. Later, Joshua Pye paints the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with paint numbers, causing dismay among the Improvers. Despite the hideous result, public sympathy turns in favor of the Improvement Society, and the community rallies around them.

label: v2 · XIII A Golden Picnic

chapter: v2 · XIII A Golden Picnic
unit: Anne and Diana meet by the stream and make plans to celebrate Anne's chosen spring birthday on Saturday. When Saturday arrives, Anne, Diana, Jane, and Priscilla go on a woods walk, naming a hidden pool and exploring back lanes. Eventually, they discover Hester Gray's forgotten garden, where Diana shares the touching romantic history of the spot.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar.
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

unit: Anne returns to Green Gables feeling disillusioned after rejecting Roy, but learns from Dorothy that he recovers quickly from heartbreak. Back in Avonlea, Anne visits Diana and her newborn baby, feeling increasingly lonely as her friends move on into new stages of life.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar.
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

value: Anne goes for an evening walk along the shore.
chapter: v4 · CHAPTER 10 LESLIE MOORE
unit: Anne goes for an evening walk along the shore and encounters Leslie Moore, whom she discovers is her striking neighbor instead of an older housewife as she had assumed. The two women converse, exchange names, and discuss their perspectives on life, though Leslie shows mixed feelings of warmth and emotional distance. Afterwards, Anne returns home to recount the surprising encounter to Gilbert.

value: Uncle Abe makes a storm prediction.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

label: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
value: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. unit: At a party, Josie Pye dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof, leading to a fall that breaks Anne's ankle. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

unit: Anne and Diana discuss Village Improvement Society plans on their drive home from Carmody when they spot a Jersey cow trampling Mr. Harrison's oat field. Believing the cow is her own nuisance Jersey, Dolly, Anne impulsively sells the stray cow on the spot to Mr. Shearer for twenty dollars. Upon returning to Green Gables, Anne discovers Dolly still in the barnyard and realizes she accidentally sold Mr. Harrison's cow, prompting her to head over to his house with the money and a cake to confess.

label: v2 · IX A Question of Color
value: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues.
chapter: v2 · IX A Question of Color
unit: Anne and Mr. Harrison debate Mrs. Lynde's virtues and discuss the village hall painting project. Later, Joshua Pye paints the hall a bright blue instead of green due to a mix-up with paint numbers, causing dismay among the Improvers. Despite the hideous result, public sympathy turns in favor of the Improvement Society, and the community rallies around them.

label: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
value: Anne is in a bad mood from a toothache.
chapter: v2 · XII A Jonah Day
unit: In a bad mood from a toothache, Anne accidentally causes fireworks to explode in the schoolroom and subsequently whips Anthony Pye after he puts a mouse in her desk. She goes home heartbroken over her bad day, but Marilla comforts her. The next morning, Anthony treats Anne with new respect, and Mrs. Rachel Lynde later confirms that the whipping gained his approval.

label: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
value: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar.
chapter: v2 · XIV A Danger Averted
unit: Mrs. Lynde tells Anne about preparations for the Ladies' Aid bazaar and asks to borrow Miss Barry's platter, while Anne learns Marilla's sight is improving. Marilla receives a letter from the twins' uncle extending their stay, and Anne remembers a conversation with Davy after catching him eating plum jam. Later, at an Village Improvement Society meeting, Gertie Pye announces that Judson Parker plans to rent his fence to a medicine company for painted ads, prompting a committee of girls to try unsuccessfully to talk him out of it.

chapter: v2 · XX The Way It Often Happens
unit: While Marilla is away, Priscilla unexpectedly arrives at Green Gables with author Mrs. Morgan and Mrs. Pendexter. label: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
value: Uncle Abe predicts a storm.
chapter: v2 · XXIV A Prophet in His Own Country
unit: Uncle Abe's storm prediction comes true with violent force, bringing a devastating hail storm to Avonlea. Anne and the twins rush home from school as Green Gables suffers broken windows and stripped vegetation. The storm kills Mr. Harrison's parrot Ginger and ruins local crops and young trees, though Gilbert and Anne find solace in the fact that Mr. Boulter's unsightly old house burned down.

label: CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde observes Matthew Cuthbert leaving Avonlea in a buggy.
chapter: CHAPTER I. Mrs. Rachel Lynde Is Surprised
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde observes a dressed-up Matthew Cuthbert leaving Avonlea in a buggy and visits Green Gables out of curiosity. Marilla Cuthbert reveals that Matthew has gone to Bright River to pick up an orphan boy they are adopting from Nova Scotia to help on the farm. Mrs. Rachel voices strong disapproval and concern over the risks of adoption before departing to spread the news.
